title: OpenPlush project document
description: Version 1 of the .plush project document (FR-070). The mesh itself is stored as a binary chunk alongside this JSON, not inline. Everything here is either user intent or a deterministic recipe for recomputation, never a cached result, so a project can never disagree with itself.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped on any breaking change. openplush-project migrates older documents forward (FR-070).

createdWith.description: Engine version that wrote this file, for diagnostics only. Never used to branch behaviour: that way lies version-sniffing.

meshChunk.description: Name of the binary chunk holding the ORIGINAL imported mesh, unrepaired. Repair is replayed from repairPlan so the source the maker supplied is never lost.

repairPlan.description: The repair choices the maker made, replayed deterministically on load. Storing the plan rather than the repaired mesh means a later engine with better repair produces a better result from the same project.

fillHoles.description: Loops the maker chose to fill. Loops absent from this list are intentional openings (FR-003; data-model section 3, step 7).

voxelRemesh.description: Opt-in last resort. Destroys UVs and sharp features, so it is never implied.

targetMm.description: Finished size along the reference dimension. Capped at 1 m: handheld-to-large plush only (FR-006, D-015).

shrinkPct.description: Uniform shrink compensation for stretch fabrics (FR-056). Uniform by design: direction-dependent compensation is out of scope (D-014).

seams.description: Seam edges keyed by SOURCE PROVENANCE, not EdgeId. EdgeIds move when repair settings change; provenance keys do not (data-model section 12).

allowanceMm.description: Per-seam override. Zero is legal only on non-fraying fabric (FR-057).

fabrics.description: Fabric profiles live IN the project (FR-050). Presets are seeds, not a shared table the project points at, so reopening a project cannot be changed by the app preset list having moved on.

fabricRegions.description: Painted regions (FR-041). Region boundaries become seams, so a piece can never span two fabrics.

directionStrokes.description: Maker strokes defining nap and grain direction (FR-051).

markings.description: Surface-attached decorations (FR-040). Stored in barycentric coordinates so they survive re-seaming and re-flattening.

detailParts.description: Components the maker marked as non-sewn (FR-005, FR-042). They produce placement marks, not pattern pieces.

pileAllowanceMultiple.description: Provisional (FR-055): the default allowance scales to at least this many times the pile length, and pieces below this multiple are flagged.

stretchMismatchThresholdPct.description: Provisional (FR-058): stretch difference across a seam that triggers a warning.

pilePrintMirrored.description: Pile fabrics print mirrored, labelled trace on wrong side (FR-054). The maker may switch to right-side printing.

acknowledgedWarnings.description: FR-064: warnings the maker has acknowledged. Keyed by code plus provenance target so an acknowledgement survives re-repair. Unacknowledged warnings are recomputed, never stored.

dismissedHints.description: Feature 002: dismissed seam-placement hints. Present in the v1 schema so feature 002 needs no migration, and so a file written by a 002-aware build still opens in a 001-only build.

cache.description: Optional, keyed by content hash, and always safe to delete. Nothing here is authoritative: a reader that ignores it computes the same result (data-model section 12).

provenanceEdge.description: Sorted pair of canonical source-vertex IDs, for example 1204:1899. Stable across changes to repair settings.

provenanceFace.description: Sorted triple of canonical source-corner IDs.

boundaryLoopRef.description: Canonical representative provenance vertex of the loop, chosen by lowest ID for determinism.

surfacePoint.description: A point ON the surface, in barycentric coordinates. Never a world-space position, which would not survive repair or rescaling.
